catalog_citation: Anderson, Stephen C. 2014. A phonological sketch of Isu. Yaounde: SIL Cameroon / Ministry of Scientific Research and Innovation. 18 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 62336; open PDF, downloaded via web.archive.org)
catalog_locator: sec. 1.13 '"Echo vowels" from imperfective suffixes', p. 11; sec. 1.9 'Unusual retroflexed allophones', p. 8; root/affix templates sec. 1.1-1.2, p. 5; tone sec. 5 / 1.17-1.18, pp. 13-14.
catalog_quote: When this Isu suffix gets added to roots lacking a C2 consonant, the vowel of the suffix merges with the vowel of the root producing a phonetically long vowel. When a C2 consonant is present in the root, this merger is blocked. Because the root syllable is always the stressed syllable in Isu, the suffix vowel is therefore unstressed. While this unstressed vowel is often a central schwa, it often takes on the character of the root vowel (thus the “echo vowel” characterization as the suffix vowel sounds like a weak echo of the main root vowel). [p. 11] ... Thus in Isu, it appears that it is only C1 central consonants that retroflex between two high /i/ vowels (or, only in stressed syllables since the first syllable of a root is always stressed). [p. 8] ... Isu roots consist of the following CV patters: (N1)C1(S1)V1(C2)(V2), i.e. an optional homorganic nasal onset to the initial consonant; an obligatory root-initial consonant, an optional semivowel, an obligatory vowel, and optional final consonants and vowels (the final root vowel is very lax ...). [p. 5, sec. 1.1] ... Isu noun prefixes and most grammatical markers are usually just an obligatory vowel preceded by an optional consonant: (C1) V1. [p. 5, sec. 1.2]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the root syllable, i.e. the first (and normally only full) syllable of the root; noun-class prefixes ((C)V) and the suffix/echo vowel after a root-final consonant are unstressed and reduced. Isu is a tone language (verbs H vs L; nouns with seven contrastive surface pitch patterns), so this is a root-prominence statement inside a tonal system, given in passing rather than in a dedicated stress section.
new_statements.exceptions: None; stated as exceptionless ('always'). Loanwords and ideophones were excluded from the database.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (root vs affixes) in citation forms from a lexical database; no phrase-level discussion; no acoustic evidence beyond the description of the unstressed echo vowel as lax/weak.
new_statements.identity_note: Anderson 2014 describes Isu of Fungom Subdivision, Menchum Division (ISO isu = isum1240) and states that no dialect differences have been noted; data from a 2,246-word lexical database built on Kießling's Toolbox corpus with two Isu Language Committee speakers. Not to be confused with Isu of Nigeria or with Aghem (aghe1239), the better-described West Ring neighbour.
